clue.text: Island capital, one on river

indicators.note: in an across clue one item placed on another comes after it, so the numeral follows the river letter

parts.note: a capital letter is a cap, as in writing something in caps
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A travel note: an island's chief city sits beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city to pair with 'Island', but it is a capital letter, a CAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is a well-known Italian holiday isle in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Mention Channel Islands military base being without leader

indicators.note: without leader means the base word loses its first letter

parts.note: a station is a military post or base

explanation.surface: A note about a Channel Islands army post that has lost its commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without leader' drops the S of STATION to give TATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A citation is a mention, such as an official mention in dispatches or a quoted reference.

clue.text: What late diner may do, coming up to hang around picnic

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper, which a late diner does
to hover is to hang about in one place

explanation.surface: Someone eating late lingers over a picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns SUP into PUS. 'picnic' means an easy task, as in 'no picnic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushover is something very easy, just as 'a picnic' is used for an easy task.

clue.text: Note double parking in priority lane done wrongly in this way?

definitions.text: Note double parking in priority lane done wrongly in this way?

indicators.note: the note and the doubled letter go inside the reworked letters
done wrongly means the letters of priority lane are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
A is a musical note

indicators.note: double means the parking letter is used twice

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Double parking in a priority lane is a motoring offence, the clue asks if that is how it was done.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: double parking in a priority lane is behaving improperly. 'done wrongly' signals the rearrangement and 'in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Double parking in a lane kept for priority traffic is acting wrongly, so it is done unsuitably.

clue.text: Fruit tree that's maintained by British for hard red fruit

indicators.note: one letter is put in place of another, the British letter standing for the hard one
read as 'that has', the tree holds the next piece within it

parts.note: the cherry is a fruit tree
to have run a business is to have maintained it, so ran
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about a fruit tree tended in Britain that bears hard red fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' works as 'that has', holding the next piece, giving CRANHERRY; 'for' then makes the swap.
explanation.definitionFit: The cranberry is a small, sharp-tasting red berry, so it is a red fruit.

clue.text: Was exultant taking over some power corruptly

indicators.note: taking over means the letters are turned over, read backwards
some means only part of the following words is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: Someone gloated after seizing a share of power by corrupt means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks WERC from 'poWER Corruptly' and 'taking over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Crew is an old past tense of crow, and to crow is to boast in triumph.

clue.text: What might have cracked open house wine after pudding

definitions.text: What might have cracked open house

indicators.note: the wine is placed after the pudding

parts.note: afters is British slang for pudding, the dessert course
hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: Someone has had the house wine after pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house wine' is a misleading phrase; 'house' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftershock is a later tremor after an earthquake, which might crack open a house.

clue.text: Be urgent, admiral, encountering disaster here?

definitions.text: Be urgent, admiral, encountering disaster here?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: meeting disaster wrecks the words, scattering their letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An admiral is urged to act fast while meeting disaster here.
explanation.walkthrough: BE stays as written at the front; 'encountering disaster' rearranges URGENT ADMIRAL into RMUDATRIANGLE. The whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bermuda Triangle is the Atlantic region notorious for ships and planes vanishing.

clue.text: Fill up again with wine without sliced bread

indicators.note: without means outside, so the wine goes round the bread

parts.note: red is wine

indicators.note: sliced means the bread word has its end cut off

parts.note: a loaf is bread

explanation.surface: Refill the glass with wine, but leave out the sliced bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliced' cuts LOAF to LOA; 'without' means outside here, not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reload is to load again, filling up once more.

clue.text: One turning out as enemy? Not 'e

definitions.text: One turning out as enemy? Not 'e

indicators.note: turning out means the letters of the words are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
'e is he with its H dropped, the letter E

explanation.surface: Is that one emerging as a foe? Certainly not him.
explanation.walkthrough: AS ENEMY rearranged gives the answer plus E, which 'Not' takes away. The whole clue also defines the answer: a yes-man is never an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man always agrees with his boss, so is never one to oppose.

clue.text: Will international cricketers think at first to trap Australia's opener?

indicators.note: the cricketers and their extra letter close around the next piece, trapping it

parts.note: players in Test matches, cricket's international fixtures, are Test men

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, here the start of Australia's
only the opening letter of the word think is wanted here

explanation.surface: Will the Test players plan in advance to get the Australian opening batsman out?
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an opener is a batsman who goes in first, which is why 'Australia's opener' reads naturally in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a will, as in 'last will and testament'.

clue.text: Regrets installing Liberal governments

indicators.note: the regrets word takes the Liberal letter into its middle, installing it there

parts.note: to rue is to regret, so rues means regrets
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in party politics

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having put Liberals into power.
explanation.definitionFit: Rules are periods of governing, as in 'years of Tory rule', so governments in that sense.

clue.text: Travelling actors needing exercise on shattering tour

indicators.note: in an across clue the exercise piece is placed on, so after, the rearranged letters
shattering breaks the word tour apart so its letters can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
PE is physical education, exercise at school

explanation.surface: Weary actors on a gruelling tour badly need some exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is only a link; 'shattering' signals the rearrangement and 'on' the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of touring performers, a group of travelling actors.

clue.text: Sensation of brother half up hidden vertical drop

parts.note: bro is a short, informal word for brother

indicators.note: only the first half of the word up, one of its two letters, is used

parts.note: a ha-ha is a sunken wall or ditch in a garden, a drop you cannot see until you reach it

explanation.surface: A dramatic story of a brother halfway up a concealed cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken fence used on British country estates so a boundary keeps livestock out without spoiling the view.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or stir, which is what a sensation causes.

clue.text: Essentially having to call wife of underground boss

parts.note: per se means intrinsically, so essentially
to phone is to call

explanation.surface: A gangster's wife essentially has to make a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underground boss' suggests a crime lord; it is Hades, ruler of the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Persephone was the wife of Hades, god of the underworld.

clue.text: It's beyond understanding where airplanes go?

definitions.meaning: something too hard to grasp is said to go this way
literally, planes pass high above a person

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means too difficult to understand, and literally describes the sky above you.

clue.text: Think it's time to go in to intervene in a dispute

indicators.note: to go in means the time letter is put inside the next word

parts.note: to mediate is to intervene to settle a dispute

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the moment has come to step in and settle an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to think deeply or reflect.

clue.text: Plan targets struggling yen

indicators.note: struggling means the word targets is thrashed about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Y is the symbol for the yen, Japan's currency

explanation.surface: A scheme aims at a weakening Japanese currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges TARGETS to STRATEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is a plan of action.

clue.text: Angry and despicable man's torn — it's one thing against another

parts.note: cross means angry
a cur is a contemptible man, from the word for a mongrel dog
rent is the old past participle of rend, so torn

explanation.surface: A furious, contemptible man has been ripped apart, an example of one thing set against another.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'man' is just a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-current flows against the main stream, and figuratively is an opposing trend.

clue.text: On a run, I cry — I show the — pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit on top of the next ones

parts.note: to sob is to cry
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: On a run, someone breaks down crying while showing the strain.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer speaks: an isobar is a line on a weather map showing pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line joining points of equal air pressure on a weather chart.

clue.text: Japanese commander nearly fired weapon

indicators.note: nearly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: shot means fired
a gun is a weapon

explanation.surface: A Japanese general almost fired his weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts SHOT to SHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was a hereditary military commander who ruled feudal Japan.

clue.text: Sleeps sound after school drink

indicators.note: the heard piece follows the school abbreviation
sound means the word for sleeps is heard rather than spelt, giving a different spelling

parts.note: naps are short sleeps

explanation.surface: A pupil sleeps soundly once school is over, then has a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'soundly', but it says the naps are heard as NAPPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong spirit, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: In windy month, briefly confined to a harbour

indicators.note: the word In is shut inside the shortened month and the article
briefly means the month name is cut short, losing its tail

parts.note: March is proverbially the windy month in Britain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A boat shut in a harbour during a blustery spring month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windy month' is March, proverbially gusty in Britain; 'briefly' trims it and 'confined to' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a harbour for yachts and small pleasure boats.

clue.text: Unexciting story gets mark for length

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of the other, the mark letter standing for the length letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
M is short for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A dull story gets a poor grade because of its length.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame means dull and lacking excitement.

clue.text: Insect has hollowed out lettuce plant

parts.note: a bug is an insect

indicators.note: hollowing out the word lettuce leaves only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A pest has eaten out the heart of a lettuce plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugle is a low-growing plant of the mint family with blue flowers.

clue.text: Variety shown by advert introduced by Old English soft drink

indicators.note: the two letters of Old English bring the other pieces in between them

parts.note: a range is a variety, as in a range of goods

explanation.surface: A selection of products, advertised in olde-worlde English, includes a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' is only a link joining RANGE to AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a sweet fizzy orange-flavoured soft drink.

clue.text: Here the English got charter to manage New York medical service finally

parts.note: to run something is to manage it

indicators.note: finally takes just the closing letter of the word service

explanation.surface: Sounds like a plan to organise New York's health system, with the English getting a charter.
explanation.walkthrough: Runnymede is the meadow on the Thames where King John sealed Magna Carta, the great English charter, in 1215.
explanation.definitionFit: Magna Carta was sealed at this Thames meadow, so it is where the English won their charter.

clue.text: Each night before the end of calendar year

parts.note: eve is the night before a festival, as in Christmas Eve

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word calendar is used

explanation.surface: Every year, on the last night of the calendar, something happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Each and every are synonyms, both meaning all taken one by one.
